Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Goal of the Game 2 Setup 3 Game Flow 4 Key Mechanics 5 Scoring & End of Game Goal of the Game In Bunny Boom, your objective is to saddle the other villagers with the rabbit problem. The player who ends the game with the fewest bunnies is the winner. Setup Each player chooses a Villager pawn and a matching Home tile. Place the center tile in the middle and put all pawns on it. Each player starts with 1 bunny on their Home tile. Create a "River" of 3 face-up cards next to the draw pile. Deal a hand of 3 cards to each player. Game Flow Villagers take turns in clockwise order. A turn consists of the following steps: Play a Card: Place one card from your hand onto the board. Phase 1: Cards are placed in lines (max 3 cards per direction) around the center. Phase 2: Cards are stacked on top of previously played cards. Activate Effect: Resolve the "Play effect" of the card you just placed. Movement: Move your pawn orthogonally to the card you just played. Activate the "Movement effect" of every card you cross. Pick up any Bunny tokens on the cards you cross and add them to your Home tile. River Effect (optional): If the card has a wave icon, you may activate one "River effect" from a card in the River and then discard it. Draw: Refill your hand to 3 cards from the deck or the River. Key Mechanics Stacking: When playing a card on top of another, you take penalty bunnies if the suits do not match. If they match, the space becomes "closed". Bunny Boom: Specific cards place tokens on the board. These must be collected by players who move across those spaces. Scoring & End of Game The game ends when the draw pile is empty or no more cards can be legally played. Count all Bunny tokens on your Home tile. Add the bunny values of the cards remaining in your hand. The player holding the Carrot token adds 4 bunnies to their total. The villager with the lowest total score wins. [Rating: 1/10] God awful.  Has the strategic level of a random take that game like exploding kittens, but with much more complex rules, so it's the worst of both worlds.

[Rating: 1/10] Holy crap this game sucks.  Its not really a game, it plays you.   There is always an obvious move, the one that gives you the least bunnies.  We spent 2/3 of the time we played looking up what the 90 icons did.  As has been pointed out there are multiple situations that the rule book does not cover.  I think Bosley will consider doing art for this game his worst career decision.  It is ten times more complex than this take that game should be.  I literally feel more ripped off by this game than I do by kickstarters that didnt ever fulfill. I would also like to point out that the two 8 ratings

[Rating: 1/10] I like the idea of the spatial considerations in a card game, but it doesn't really work in the form it is now. I don't mind take that in a take that game. This game is a pain to teach, symbology is horrible, several rules are just confusing. The rules give you a procedural turn structure, but then tell you to turn that structure on it's head when playing certain cards.   This design needed a few more years of development and streamlining to be fun.

[Rating: 2/10] Played at "Salon du jeu et du jouet", the game is a take-that with no positive interaction, very chaotic, and I didn't enjoy my play of it. There isn't enough thinking to be interesting, and it is slightly too complex to be a light game to play with younger people in my family. I would rather get a game like exploding kitten if I wanted random take that.

[Rating: 2/10] I want to be clear from the start: I never enjoy pouring scorn on someone’s labour of love. I know how hard it is to make a game, getting an idea through development, art, production, and fulfilment is no small feat. But Bunny Boom is, unfortunately, substandard on almost every front; with one sincere exception: the bunny-shaped meeples are genuinely cute.  Where things fall down is everywhere else.
